title: Finite Laurent-polynomial open atlas for a locally split reductive group
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. An $A$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $H$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme whose geometric fibres are reductive: each is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $S\hookrightarrow H$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], with a specified isomorphism $S\simeq\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$, $r\geq0$, whose geometric fibres are maximal tori; a torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$, and maximal means maximal for subgroup inclusion. Here $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$, with multiplication of units. Then there are an integer $d\geq0$, a nonempty finite index set $I$, and $A$-morphisms
$$\theta_i:\operatorname{Spec}A[x_1,\ldots,x_d,z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]\longrightarrow H\qquad(i\in I)$$
which are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and whose images cover the underlying space of $H$. The spectrum and its contravariant functoriality are those of [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; the displayed algebra is the polynomial algebra in the $x_j$ and invertible variables $z_l$. The cases $d=0$ and $r=0$ use empty lists of variables.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Definition 5.1.1 and discussion (printed p.136), Corollary 5.1.11 (pp.142-143), Theorem 5.1.13 (pp.143-144); finite translated-cell cover is the agent-formulated consequence of the relative open cell and geometric Bruhat charts. For the field charts see Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017), Theorems 21.73 and 21.84 (printed pp.447 and 451). Original Conrad PDF WANTED locally; no Stacks tag supplies relative reductive-group structure.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-split-root-data-weyl-lifts] to $A,H,S$: it supplies one finite root set $\Phi$, a positive system $\Phi^+$, parametrizations $u_\alpha$, the finite group $W$ and representatives $n_w\in H(A)$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-root-product-open-cell] to these data. Write $N=|\Phi^+|$ and retain its $U^-,U^+,B$ and open immersion $j:U^-\times_AS\times_AU^+\to H$. Both inputs require exactly the local Noetherian and geometric reductivity hypotheses already assumed; neither requires a henselian ring nor an algebraically closed residue field.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, introduction to Section 4, printed p.107 (weight subbundles); Definition 5.1.1 and its following discussion, p.136 (connected-base constancy); Theorem 4.1.4, p.110 (relative root groups); Proposition 5.1.6, p.138 (constant Weyl group); Corollary 5.1.11, pp.142-143 (global Weyl representatives). Local freeness of root lines becomes freeness over the local ring. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Fix enumerations of $\Phi^+$ and $-\Phi^+$. The root parametrizations and ordered product isomorphisms identify the source of $j$ with $\mathbf A_A^N\times_AS\times_A\mathbf A_A^N$. Its coordinate algebra is $A[x_1,\ldots,x_{2N},z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$: a map out is precisely two lists of $N$ arbitrary elements and $r$ units; the inverse identification reads off these coordinates. Thus this is an isomorphism $c:V\to U^-\times_AS\times_AU^+$. For $w\in W$ define $\theta_w=L_{n_w}\circ j\circ c$, where $L_{n_w}(h)=n_wh$. Its inverse translation is $L_{n_w^{-1}}$, by the group identities. Hence $\theta_w$ identifies $V$ with the open subscheme $n_w\Omega$, where $\Omega=j(U^-\times_AS\times_AU^+)$; it is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem 5.1.13 and proof, printed pp.143-144 (ordered positive root products, closed Borel and relative open cell), with Theorem 4.1.4 for root parametrizations. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. Geometric Borel terminology agrees with Milne, Algebraic Groups (2017), 21.32 and 21.68.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $F$ and $A\to F$. The relative inputs identify $S_F$ as a split maximal torus, $B_F$ as its positive Borel, and $U_F^+$ as its unipotent radical. They identify $W$ with the geometric Weyl group and $n_w$ with a system of representatives. The stratification and multiplication isomorphisms in [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] therefore give, for each $g\in H(F)$, some $w\in W$ and $u\in U_F^+(F),\ b\in B_F(F)$ with $g=u n_w b$. Indeed its stratum coordinate lies in the subscheme $V^w\subseteq U_F^+$, which suffices here.

source.place: Theorem 21.73(a), p.447, and Theorem 21.68(a), Remark 21.69, pp.445-446; explicit root-coordinate argument for the translated-cell cover.

proof.text: Conjugation by $n_w^{-1}$ carries $B_F$ and its radical to $B'=n_w^{-1}B_Fn_w$ and $U'=n_w^{-1}U_F^+n_w$. Its positive roots are $w^{-1}\Phi^+$ by the root conjugation formula of step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] to this Borel, enumerating its roots with the members of $-\Phi^+$ first and those of $\Phi^+$ last. It expresses $n_w^{-1}u n_w$ as $v_-v_+$, where each factor in $v_-$ belongs to a negative root subgroup and each factor in $v_+$ belongs to a positive root subgroup. The subgroup inclusions of step 1 give $v_-\in U_F^-(F)$ and $v_+\in U_F^+(F)$. Since $B_F=S_F\ltimes U_F^+$, write $v_+b=st$ with $s\in S_F(F)$ and $t\in U_F^+(F)$. Consequently $g=n_w v_-st\in n_w\Omega(F)$. This uses arbitrary-order product coordinates, not commutativity of the root groups.

source.place: Theorem 21.73(a), p.447, and Theorem 21.68(a), Remark 21.69, pp.445-446; explicit root-coordinate argument for the translated-cell cover.

proof.text: Let $h$ be any underlying point of $H$, and let $F$ be an algebraic closure of its residue field $\kappa(h)$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(h)\to H$ is an $F$-point over the induced $A\to F$ and has image $h$. Steps 3-4 put this point in some $n_w\Omega$; composing its factorization through this open subscheme shows $h\in|n_w\Omega|$. Thus the images of the $\theta_w$ cover every point of $H$. Take $I=W$ and $d=2N$. A finite group contains its identity, so $I$ is nonempty. Empty root and torus coordinate lists cause no change: when $\Phi$ is empty the same Bruhat argument has $W=\{1\}$, and the single chart covers.

source.place: Theorem 21.73(a), p.447, and Theorem 21.68(a), Remark 21.69, pp.445-446; explicit root-coordinate argument for the translated-cell cover.

proof_origin.place: 21.68(a), 21.69 and 21.73(a); assembly with Conrad relative structural inputs. The Weyl translated-cell cover is proved here by reordered root factors, not assumed from the field chart cover.
